lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Daisy! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the soda swap went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Lots of celebrations this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: We had a birthday party, there was so much food. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It feels like a lot right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I really want to feel like myself again. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You said the same thing last week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really like my Coke with lunch.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That Coke is part of your routine, and giving it up feels like losing something.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to swap soda for water on 5 days next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If letting go of the Coke gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll keep some fruit cut up in the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 0 out of 5 days, the hard part was letting go of the Coke, and next week you're going to swap soda for water on 5 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Heat discomfort is minor; no same-day action needed.
Reports not doing swap; water unappealing.
Motivation: wants to avoid cancer recurrence.
Praise slightly generous given 0 of 5 days.
Guilt and party food as barriers.
Fatigue as reason to hold off.
Knee pain as reason not to walk.
Wants to feel like herself; open to liking new habits.
Confrontational reminder of prior missed goal.
Sets goal unilaterally without asking her input.

flags.reason: 'You have to make this a priority' pushes advice without permission and ignores ambivalence.
Reminds participant of prior missed goal; confrontational rather than exploring barriers.
Repeats seltzer suggestion after participant already rejected it at line 7 and ignored it at line 19.
'I really want to feel like myself again' was not reflected; coach moved to autonomy statement instead of deepening it.
Verbatim repeat of line 44 suggests scripted or disengaged response to 'I don't know'.
Goal of 5 days set unilaterally without asking participant's preferred target after she expressed uncertainty.

score.summary: Coach reviewed last week's goal and built a backup plan, and summarized well at the end. However, the coach repeatedly persuaded and repeated the seltzer suggestion, and set the 5-day goal without the participant's input, which undercut partnership despite her clear change talk about wanting to feel like herself again.
strengths: Line 8 and line 42: complex reflections captured ambivalence and the emotional weight of giving up Coke.
Line 37: asked permission before offering the seltzer idea.
Line 55: open question about a backup plan (participant offered fruit at line 56).
Line 57: clear summary of the week and new goal, with a chance for correction.
coaching_tips: Line 33 and 35: replace 'You have to make this a priority' with an open question about what matters to her, e.g., 'What would make this feel worth the effort?'
Line 39: don't repeat the seltzer idea; she already declined it at line 7. Ask 'What else have you thought about trying?' instead.
Line 31: reflect her change talk ('You want to feel like yourself again') and ask what that would look like before moving on.
Line 51: ask 'How many days next week feels doable for you?' before stating a target.
Line 48: avoid verbatim repeats; when she says 'I don't know' at line 47, explore with a reflection or open question.
